title: "Money-Printing Machine"
author: Jack242
selftext:
Is it just me, or is it kind of funny seeing people post here that they spent 6 months building a trading bot that makes 30% a year?

The Nasdaq is up around 30% this year. 😅

Rule #1: if you've actually found a profitable strategy, managed to automate it, and it consistently outperforms the major indexes over the long run, the last thing you should be doing is posting about it all over Reddit or trying to sell the bot.

If you've really built a money-printing machine, why would you risk ruining your own edge?

At this point, I don't really see much difference between people selling trading courses and people promoting the "amazing" trading bots they built.

comments.author: Tripple_sneeed
comments.body:
The people trying to sell these products are grifting, yeah, that is obvious.

  
That being said, the value in a strategy that returns 30% is that it's almost certainly doing it with a return per exposure hour higher than buy and hold. Buying QQQ and holding it means that you're using your capital 100% of the time to get that 30%. A strategy that returns 30% while holding an average of \~an hour per trading session is extremely powerful because it means that you can use the other 7 hours for other strategies, and even if you aren't stacking multiple strategies you have less exposure potential for black swan events. 

  
Think about having two, three, four strategies that are each returning 30% AGR and how quickly that growth compounds.
